claim_being_audited: The actor recommends certifying the model for launch on the theory that aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public AI-governance guidance are sufficient despite an unresolved underperforming named launch use case and an open legal question about required disclosure.
decision_criteria: Whether the affected weakness is material under policy because it affects a named launch use case or customer commitment.
Whether the required disclosure obligation has been satisfied before launch.
Whether an approved risk acceptance exists that expressly covers launching without prior resolution.
Whether the actor's conclusion depends on product framing or general guidance rather than admissible policy-satisfying evidence.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the childcare subsidy eligibility gap must be disclosed before launch.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering this specific named launch use case, if certification is to proceed without prior resolution.
The actual pre-launch disclosure or model-card text showing the limitation was disclosed as required.
Authoritative evidence that the affected segment is no longer a named launch use case or no longer part of county commitments, if that is the basis for non-materiality.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the childcare subsidy eligibility segment misses target and is a named launch use case in two county rollout commitments.
The governing policy states material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review is still open on whether the gap must be disclosed, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance, a completed disclosure, or a final legal determination.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not resolve the disclosure obligation for a material named use case.
Public NIST/model-card guidance is general governance context, not evidence that this specific certification satisfies the release policy.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
Any claim that the 7% projected traffic label resolves materiality for a named launch use case.
Any claim that general public AI risk-management or model-card guidance substitutes for the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implicit claim that the open legal review can be treated as satisfied for launch approval.
